current_text: EAST BRIDGE

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Not grown yet? Plant a Magic Bean at the mound beside it.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE NORTH BANK

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Welcome to the far side. The wall of tyres ahead has three gaps. One has been plugged with junk.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE JUNK DAM

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Somebody has dumped half a landfill across the feeder channel.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Needs a charging mount. Brother Bramble will pay.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: GIDEON THE GIANT GOAT

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Eats anything. Climbs anything. Rams anything.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Do not feed him the sign.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: JUNK BARRICADE

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A pile of tyres, doors and ambition across the gap.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Landfill Depths are beyond. Bring something that charges.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: RUST PEAK YARDS

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Where the best rust in the kingdom is made. Handmade. Small batch.
new_text: The finest rust in the kingdom. Small batch. Very slow finish.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE LANDFILL DEPTHS

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Three levels. Mandatory. Bring a nose peg.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Do not dig deeper than the raccoons.
new_text: Do not dig deeper than the raccoons. They will consider it competitive.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE ROTHEART

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The source of the sickness. Do not enter. Do not breathe deeply. Do not lick anything.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The deeper you go, the more it grows.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE ROTHEART

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Source of the sickness, now closed for healing. The vines are only vines. Mostly. Visitors welcome.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: NOTE FROM A DRUID

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The door is warm because something in there is thriving. It is thriving very, very hard. It is thriving at us. Please do not open it.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: NOTE FROM A DRUID

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The door is warm because the compost is happy. The compost was always happy. We just forgot what that looked like.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE SEED SHRINE

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Plant a seed in a plot and it flips that plot and its four neighbours.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Bring every plot into bloom to wake the great beanstalk.

current_text: THE SCREE FIELDS

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Loose rubble, jagged tin and thistles. Impassable on foot.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Mounts only. Boots are not covered.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: SCREE RULES

speaker: (narration)
current_text: No walking. No dismounting. No dropping your lunch.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The scree will find it.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: TODAY'S JUNK

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Tyres, fridges, one (1) piano.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Nothing goes to waste. Everything goes to the Dump.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: NOTE

speaker: (narration)
current_text: I put the good stuff in the hollow log. If you are reading this, you are standing too close to the good stuff.
new_text: Good stuff in the hollow log. If you can read this, kindly take one step back from my retirement.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: - a raccoon

speaker: (check key)
current_text: A trash golem the size of a shed, with a coat of moss and a fridge for a body. Something is growing out of its ears. It has stopped having opinions about recycling and started having opinions about you.
new_text: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. This is no place for a cool head.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: A scarecrow druid with a wreath, a grudge, and a cabbage growing where its heart should be. The crows left. The seeds are still angry.
new_text: A scarecrow druid faces you, a cabbage growing where its heart should be. You see no crows. The garden has bigger problems.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Four junk gulls in a trench coat, if the trench coat were made of screaming and mutated fungus. They stole a can and they are not sharing. The can is growing mushrooms.
new_text: Four junk gulls guard a stolen can, shrieking over its crop of mushrooms. You have interrupted a very small turf war.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Welcome to the Compost Grange. Brother Bramble, Warden of the Stream. Please close the door behind you. And lock it. And check the window.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals eat the kingdom's garbage and turn it into fertilizer, and our magic helps the crops grow.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Our magic runs through nature itself, and {villain} used it against us. Our Archdruid, Compostella, went first. Something got into her roots.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Now nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil. Everything is too alive, and the whole Dump is sick with growing. Also, SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Back at the Grange? Good. Sort your boots on the way in: compost, metal, glass, paper. And check them for tendrils.
new_text: Back at the Grange? Sort your boots: compost, metal, glass, paper. Check for tendrils. We already have enough houseplants.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The Archdruid planted a tree for every royal birthday. There is a row of them past the stream. Eleven trees. Then nothing.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: I water the twelfth spot anyway. I couldn't tell you why. It feels as if somebody is still coming.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Not long ago, somebody carried a sleeping young man through these woods at night. He glowed, faintly. Four colours.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The raccoons saw. Raccoons see everything.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: I never thought I'd say it: the Dump is healing. The vines are only vines, the mushrooms are only mushrooms, and the Archdruid is herself again. She is mortified.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Breathe in. Go on. You may breathe deeply now. That smell is honest compost.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: This morning Compostella walked straight to the row of royal trees and planted a twelfth. She didn't say why.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: She just smiled at you on the way past.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The stream is clean, the fields are calm and the zucchini has gone back to being a zucchini. Thank you. We owe you more than compost.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Though NOBODY has explained who ate it. The raccoons have gone very quiet.
new_text: Though NOBODY has explained who ate the compost. The raccoons have suddenly become excellent listeners.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Granny Gristle, junk-trader! Born in a haybale, raised in a barn, retired to a shed. This is the shed. It's started growing. It's got a window I never put in.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Everything here's Refusemancer-issue: grown, composted, well rinsed. Found, not stolen, dearie. The raccoon found it. I just held it very tightly.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Strong cards, solid cards, cards with a faint smell of earth. And a faint hum. Don't ask about the hum.
new_text: Cards grown strong, rinsed well, faint smell of earth. Hear that hum? Well, I never promised a silent auction. Heh!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Shop's open, dearie! The turnips are a day old, which makes them better.
new_text: Shop's open, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: They're also looking at me, which makes them worse. Heh!
new_text: They're looking at me again. I prefer a root vegetable that minds its own business. Heh!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Granny Gristle, junk-trader! The shed is just a shed again. The turnips are only turnips.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: I had a little cry, then I planted a field. Shop's open, dearie. Welcome back to the sane side of farming. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Shop's open! The turnips are a day old, and they're not looking at anybody. I checked. Twice.
new_text: Shop's open! Day-old turnips. None looking at anybody. Finally, produce that knows when to look away. Heh!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Oh good, a pair of legs! Wren Muckfoot, animal handler. I speak fluent goat. It's mostly screaming. Lately it's about the plants: the fields keep trying to eat my herd.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: The boar and the goat in the stables will carry you if you ask nicely. Or rudely. They're not picky, and they're about the only things here that haven't gone strange.
new_text: The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely. Ask rudely. They don't speak either. Good, sensible animals.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Any luck with the herd? Look for the goat first. It'll be eating something it shouldn't. If the thing is eating it back, shout.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Wren Muckfoot, animal handler! The herd's back, and the goat's eating a sign.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: The sign's not eating back. I've never been so happy to see a goat ruin something.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Every animal present and entirely un-mutated. I could cry. I might.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Into a bucket. For the plants.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Three of my animals got out: a goat, a pig and a raccoon with a briefcase. The Rot's in the fields and they're wandering right into it.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Find each one out in the Dump and walk it back towards the pen before dark. Don't chase. Walk firmly. Make eye contact.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Animals respect eye contact. Raccoons respect cash.
new_text: Animals respect eye contact. Raccoons consider it the start of negotiations.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: Three escapees, out in the fields. The goat is eating something. The pig is in a puddle. The raccoon is writing a strongly worded letter.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: All three home! The pen's never looked so full. Here's your reward.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: It's a card. It's a goat. It's a goat you can play.
new_text: A goat card. You can play this one without having to catch it afterwards.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Wren Muckfoot
current_text: The herd's home and it's plotting. Thanks! Druid Sorrel at the centre bridge will grow you a crossing now. Tell her I sent you.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Now then, fertilizer. The crops are sulking and the soil's gone strange, and good clean fertilizer is the one thing the Rot can't grow in.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: I need three sacks from around the Dump. They're lying where the animals left them. Don't ask how. I never have. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Three sacks of fertilizer, dearie. Try the fields, the east edge and the far side of the stream. Follow your nose. Then apologise to it.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Three whole sacks! The crops are going to sing. Not literally.

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: Mostly not. Here's your reward. Found, not stolen. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
current_text: The fields are fed. Want to plant your own? A sack of fertilizer and a little patience. The patience I can't sell you.
new_text: The fields are fed. Plant your own with a sack of fertilizer and a little patience. Can't sell you patience. Nobody stays to browse it.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Somebody dumped a dam of junk across the feeder channel on the north bank, and the stream cannot breathe. Borrow a mount from the stables, charge the dam, and my compost boots are yours.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The junk dam on the north bank. Ride the goat from the north stable and charge it. Do not slow down. Dams can smell hesitation.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The stream is flowing! It is practically dancing. Here: compost boots, still warm. They squelch with pride.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The stream is clear. For now. The kingdom will refill it by Thursday. That is why we are here.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Ah, a visitor. Druid Thistlewick, Keeper of the Dump's Questions. I have sat in this ring of old appliances for forty years.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: The dishwasher and I have an understanding. Lately, the dishwasher has started talking back.
new_text: The dishwasher and I have an understanding. Lately it talks back. Forty years, and NOW it wants to clear the air.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Four questions about the Refusemancers, their work and their oath. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Verdant Dump.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Sort your thoughts like your bins: compost, recycle, regret. Answer well for gold and seeds. Answer poorly for a gentle, rustling sigh.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Back to improve your score? Good. A druid is just a student who never left the garden.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Zero. Remarkable in its way. Nothing for you.
new_text: Zero. We have found room for growth. Rather a lot of room. No reward this time.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: The signs are patient. I am slightly less so. The dishwasher is not patient at all.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: One. A single seed. Plant it, water it, and try again.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Two. Half-grown. A fine place to start. The rest will sprout.
new_text: Two. Half-grown. Keep tending those thoughts; we are not harvesting excuses.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Three! Nearly in bloom. Take your reward and a sprig of mint.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: FOUR! A perfect harvest! You may now call yourself a Certified Refusemancer, First Class.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: The reward is real. The certificate is compostable. The earth thanks you, quietly. The dishwasher, loudly.
new_text: Your reward is real. The certificate is compostable. When you tire of showing it off, let it become something humble.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Another round! The Dump pays a small fee for repeat scholarship.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
current_text: Not a pass. Walk the Verdant Dump, read the signs, and come back. There is no limit on attempts.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: Step RIGHT up to the County Fair's own SORT IT OUT! I'm Recycle Rhonda: fair judge, pie inspector, and the finest dumpster-diver in three counties!

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: Back in the nineties I was the voice of Captain Compost Badger and his Sorting Squad, on between the cartoons. Nobody knew. The badger had a cape.
new_text: I voiced Captain Compost Badger and his Sorting Squad back in the nineties! Nobody knew! All that fame went to a badger in a cape!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: The Rot cancelled the pumpkin contest. It can't cancel ME! Today's show: twenty pieces of junk, one conveyor, four bins. Compost, metal, glass or paper!

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: Send each piece to the right bin before it falls off the end. Rewards by performance, plus a first-time bonus. Gloves on!

current_text: Twenty pieces of junk ride the conveyor. Send the front piece to the right bin (click a bin, or keys 1-4 or the arrow keys) before it reaches the end. A wrong bin or a miss breaks your streak. A long streak scores more.

new_text: BLUE RIBBON sorting! Reduce! Reuse! Refuse to quit! All three goats in the crowd are cheering. Or hungry.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: Your very first run at the fair! Here's your bonus, free, no obligation. It's a salve.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: The salve is made of compost. It works. Don't ask.
new_text: Compost salve! Rub it in! The salve, champ. Not the victory.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: Not quite a run, champ. That's fine. The belt isn't going anywhere.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
current_text: Unlike the jam jar. The jam jar went everywhere.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Twenty-five plots of garden sit in a five-by-five square, some bare and some in bloom. Plant a seed in a plot and that plot and its four neighbours flip between bare and bloom. Bring every plot into bloom to wake the great beanstalk.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Work from the top row down: if the plot above a bare plot is bare, plant right below it. Then fix the last row with the first row. Count your seeds; there are only four solutions.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Every plot blooms at once. The beanstalk rises, shakes out a seed pouch the size of a satchel, and hands it down with a leaf. It is still warm.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: The garden is in full bloom. Nothing left to plant.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: WARNING: THE ROT

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Plants here are unnaturally alive. Fungi mutate. Roots invade structures, hands, and lunch.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Do not feed anything. Do not name anything. Do not turn your back on the zucchini.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE ROT: CURED

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The plants here are only naturally alive, mostly. The zucchini has been spoken to.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE CORRUPTION SPREADS FROM THE NORTH

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Whatever our Archdruid has become, it is feeding the whole Dump.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Follow the dying fields. Then follow the living ones. They are worse.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: THE ARCHDRUID IS BACK

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Archdruid Compostella is recovering. She asks that you not call her "the Rotheart Archdruid" at breakfast.
